verses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ وَٱلنَّٰزِعَٰتِ غَرْقًا
verses.translation: By those [angels] who extract with violence[1833]
verses.footnotes: [1833]- i.e., those who tear out the souls of those destined for Hell.

verses.translation: And [by] those who remove with ease[1834]
verses.footnotes: [1834]- i.e., those angels who ease out the souls of those destined for Paradise.

verses.translation: And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming[1835]
And those who race each other in a race[1836]
verses.footnotes: [1836]- Racing to deliver the souls of the believers to Paradise.

verses.translation: And those who arrange [each] matter,[1837]
On the Day the blast [of the Horn] will convulse [creation],

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.translation: There will follow it the subsequent [one].

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.translation: Hearts,[1838] that Day, will tremble,
verses.footnotes: [1838]- Those of the disbelievers who denied the Resurrection.

verses.translation: Their eyes[1839] humbled.

segments.description: Active participle — nominative, feminine, singular, indefinite

verses.translation: They are [presently] saying, "Will we indeed be returned to [our] former state [of life]?

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.translation: Even if we should be decayed bones?"[1840]
verses.footnotes: [1840]- The disbelievers say this in ridicule of the warning.

verses.translation: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."[1841]
verses.footnotes: [1841]- i.e., "If that were so, we would not be able to escape punishment."

verses.translation: Indeed, it will be but one shout,
And suddenly they will be [alert] upon the earth's surface.
Has there reached you the story of Moses? -

verses.arabic: إِذْ نَادَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
verses.translation: When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā,
"Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.

verses.arabic: فَقُلْ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
verses.translation: And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, subjunctive, 2nd person, masculine, singular

verses.translation: And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'"

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, subjunctive, 2nd person, masculine, singular

verses.translation: And he showed him the greatest sign,[1842]
verses.footnotes: [1842]- i.e., the miracle of his staff becoming a great snake.

verses.translation: But he [i.e., Pharaoh] denied and disobeyed.
Then he turned his back, striving [i.e., plotting].[1843]
verses.footnotes: [1843]- An alternative meaning is "running [from the snake]."

verses.translation: And he gathered [his people] and called out
And said, "I am your most exalted lord."
So Allāh seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression].[1844].
verses.footnotes: [1844]- i.e., for Pharaoh's setting himself up as a deity and for his previous oppression of the people and denial of Moses.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰٓ
verses.translation: Indeed in that is a lesson [i.e., warning] for whoever would fear [Allāh].

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.arabic: ءَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بَنَىٰهَا
verses.translation: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? He [i.e., Allāh] constructed it.
He raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.[1845]
verses.footnotes: [1845]- i.e., created the day from within the surrounding darkness.

verses.translation: And after that He spread the earth.
He extracted from it its water and its pasture,
And the mountains He set firmly
As enjoyment [i.e., provision] for you and your grazing livestock.
But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity[1846] -
The Day when man will remember that for which he strove,

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.translation: And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see -

segments.description: Verb — perfect, 3rd person, feminine, singular, passive
Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.translation: So as for he who transgressed
And preferred the life of the world,
Then indeed, Hellfire will be [his] refuge.

verses.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ
verses.translation: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord[1847] and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,
Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.
They ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?[1848]

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.translation: In what [position] are you that you should mention it?[1849]
verses.footnotes: [1849]- Meaning that Muḥammad (ﷺ) had no knowledge of it, so how could he inform them?

verses.translation: To your Lord is its finality.[1850]
verses.footnotes: [1850]- i.e., its destination and termination. And to Him belongs ultimate knowledge of it.

verses.translation: You are only a warner for those who fear it.

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.arabic: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوٓا۟ إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا
verses.translation: It will be, on the Day they see it,[1851] as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural
Verb — imperfect, jussive, 3rd person, masculine, plural
